meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-25 | Time: 10:00 PT | Duration: 60m | Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (Nimbus, ML Eng), Carlos Rivera (Nimbus, CTO), Priya Das (Nimbus, SRE), Evan Liu (Nimbus, Product)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review INT8 vs FP8 quantization results. INT8 shows 2.4x throughput improvement and ~30% cost reduction vs FP16 baseline but with measurable QA regressions on a small subset of prompts. FP8 offers similar perf to INT8 for some model variants but introduced stability issues on longer contexts. Agreed next steps: rerun INT8 on 16k context, run on Dedicated nodes for throughput baseline, deliver FP8 stability fixes and share benchmark spreadsheet and security artifacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick roll call and then we'll dive into the quant results. uh Jordan, you want to kick us off with the high level?
[00:18] Jordan Patel: yeah hi, good morning. so we ran the INT8 and FP8 passes across your test suite last week. overall INT8 gave around 2.4x throughput on the 8k context baseline and about a 28-32% token-cost reduction compared to FP16. caveat, there were some quality diffs on the summarization and code generation tests.
[00:39] Sofia Martinez: can you be more specific on the quality diffs? like are we seeing hallucinations or style shifts?
[00:47] Jordan Patel: mostly hallucination increases in very narrow prompts, also some tokenization edge cases where the model produces truncated code blocks. we flagged about 12 prompts out of 1.2k where the perf was unacceptable.
[01:02] Carlos Rivera: when you say truncated, is that related to KV cache issues? we saw some earlier notes about KV cash mismatches with quantized kernels.
[01:12] Maya Singh: yeah there can be KV cache alignment issues, especially when kernels are fused differently in INT8 paths. sometimes attention states round differently, which can cause off-by-one in continuation. we saw that in one FP8 run too. it's an area we can mitigate with a tiny compatibility shim.
[01:28] Priya Das: ok, stability is a big flag for us. if FP8 is flaky for longer sequences, we can't move to that for production. what was the context length in the tests?
[01:36] Jordan Patel: most tests were 8k. we did a small 12k run with FP8 and saw increased error rates and out-of-memory on the smallest nodes. we didn't push INT8 to 16k yet, that's on the to-do list.
[01:50] Evan Liu: curious about latency percentiles. throughput is great but p99 latency for interactive workflows matters. how did INT8 affect tail latencies?
[01:58] Jordan Patel: median improved substantially, p95 improved too, but p99 had a modest increase in jitter for some requests because of kernel fallbacks when sequences cross boundary conditions. we think Dedicated nodes will smooth that out.
[02:12] Alex Kim: that ties into the cost/latency tradeoff we discussed earlier — Dedicated for stable p99, Hosted to prototype. Carlos, are you still leaning Dedicated for the pilot?
[02:21] Carlos Rivera: yes, for customer-facing inference we want isolation and predictable SLOs. we're open to a hybrid: start hosted for evaluation, then Dedicated for the pilot.
[02:30] Sofia Martinez: can you share the concrete numbers for token cost delta? we need it for internal modeling.
[02:35] Jordan Patel: sure, sample: FP16 baseline cost/unit 1.0; INT8 approx 0.72 token-cost; FP8 fluctuated 0.65-0.78 depending on model variant and per-token stability tuning. these are rough and we will add the full spreadsheet.
[02:53] Priya Das: on the security side, we need to see audit logs for quantized deployments and KMS integration notes.
[02:59] Maya Singh: yes we'll share our audit log example and SSO/SAML screenshots. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments, and Dedicated nodes can be put into your VPC.
[03:12] Carlos Rivera: any regulatory issues with moving FP8/INT8 model weights into our environment?
[03:17] Alex Kim: weights are not exported in Private or Dedicated — it's a serving runtime. but we'll send a security whitepaper to confirm.
[03:25] Jordan Patel: quick note on perf: quantization gains are workload-dependent. seq length distribution, batch sizes, and prompt shapes matter. we saw best gains on high-throughput short-turn dialogue loads. code gen with long outputs had more regressions.
[03:45] Sofia Martinez: about the 12 failing prompts, can we get a list and reproduce locally? we want to test mitigation strategies like prompt rewrite or token bucket.
[03:53] Jordan Patel: yes we'll send the failing prompt IDs and a sample payload. also include the model variant, quant config file, and trace ids.
[04:02] Evan Liu: FP8 sounded promising cost-wise but stability worries me. is there a plan to backport fixes or use mixed precision?
[04:10] Maya Singh: we've been experimenting with mixed FP8/INT8 paths where sensitive layers stay in FP16. that reduces the stability hit but loses some perf. it's a tuning knob.
[04:22] Carlos Rivera: for Dedicated runs, what's the expected provisioning lead time?
[04:26] Alex Kim: typically 3-5 business days once we lock a window, quicker if we have a reserved pool. for pilot we can spin up a temporary Dedicated cluster for a two-week validation.
[04:38] Priya Das: can we schedule an on-site perf run with our infra team? we need to see real network topology and VPC egress.
[04:45] Alex Kim: yes, we'll coordinate. action item: Alex to set up dedicated window.
[04:50] Sofia Martinez: also want to confirm the eval harness — are you using the same tokenizer and sampling settings as our production? differences can cause apparent regressions.
[04:59] Jordan Patel: we tried to match settings but there were a couple mismatches (beam width and stop tokens). we'll normalize and rerun.
[05:08] Carlos Rivera: for rollback strategies, how does Redwood handle model fallback when quantized variant fails quality checks in-flight?
[05:16] Maya Singh: we have smart routing — can route to FP16 or different model variants based on per-route quality signals. we can also do A/B and automatic fallback if the quality metric dips.
[05:27] Evan Liu: what's the QA metric you're using for automatic fallback? perplexity or more task-specific metric?
[05:32] Jordan Patel: both; perplexity is quick but we rely on task-specific eval like BLEU for code or ROUGE for summarization. we also track post-inference heuristics like completion length and stop-token ratios.
[05:46] Sofia Martinez: timeline question: assuming fixes, when could we put INT8 into a small pilot?
[05:52] Alex Kim: if Jordan reruns 16k tests next week and Dedicated window happens in ~2 weeks, we could be in a small pilot by mid-April.
[06:00] Carlos Rivera: ok that works. any blockers on our side for the Dedicated run? Priya?
[06:05] Priya Das: just the VPC peering and firewall rules; we'll need Redwood IP ranges and an implementation checklist.
[06:12] Maya Singh: I'll send the VPC peering doc and IP lists as part of the security packet.
[06:18] Alex Kim: great. last bit — cost modeling for customers: we can provide token-level cost breakout and predicted monthly burn for your expected QPS. would that help?
[06:27] Evan Liu: yes please, include a couple scenarios.
[06:30] Alex Kim: ok to recap next steps...
[06:33] Jordan Patel: to recap, I'll rerun INT8 on 16k and send raw logs + failing prompt list by Monday 2026-03-29.
[06:40] Alex Kim: I'll coordinate Dedicated window and schedule an on-site perf run by 2026-04-05.
[06:44] Maya Singh: I'll share security artifacts (audit log sample, SSO flow, IP ranges) by 2026-03-30.
[06:50] Sofia Martinez: I'll provide the 3 worst-case prompts by 2026-03-27.
[06:54] Carlos Rivera: sounds good. thanks team.
[06:57] Alex Kim: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in Slack and send the spreadsheet. end of call.
notes: References: shared benchmark spreadsheet (link in Slack), config file quant-config-v2.json, security pack v2. Attendees asked for Dedicated perf window and audit logs. Some transcription artifacts: 'KV cash' instead of KV cache, occasional speaker attribution issues.
